title: XVII–XXI: general and special governance; merely corporeal creatures
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Matthew 5:45; 10:29 — Deuteronomy 28; Psalm 104; 146:6–9; Psalm 147; Isaiah 42:5; Acts 14:15–17; Job 36–41; Proverbs 6:6–8; Jeremiah 5:22; 8:7; Jonah 4:7 — one again he rules as things without sense, another as sensing things — so nevertheless he governs that what was given toward them in that he either conserves or exalts or depresses them — XXI. Merely corporeal creatures God governs less laboriously indeed. XX. And it is belonging toward merely corporeal creatures, or corporeal plus incorporeal together, or incorporeal simply, whether belonging toward angels plus humans. XIX. SPECIAL governance is that by which God governs singular things conveniently toward their natures. XVIII. GENERAL governance is that by which God governs universal things commonly. XVII. Third, it is general or special.
pass_b_english: XVII. Third, governance is general or special. XVIII. GENERAL governance is that by which God governs all things in common. It is also called universal, and likewise common providence; and this does not admit of more and less.

XIX. SPECIAL governance is that by which God governs singular things as befits their natures. This is also called singular providence, and it has certain grades of its own. XX. And it is of merely corporeal creatures, or of corporeal and incorporeal together, or of the incorporeal simply — that is, of angels and of humans.

XXI. Merely corporeal creatures God governs with less labor, yet so that what was given them He either conserves in them, or raises, or brings low; some again He rules as things without sense, others as things that sense. Compare Deuteronomy 28; Psalm 104; 146:6–9; Psalm 147 throughout; Isaiah 42:5; Acts 14:15–17; Job 36–41; Proverbs 6:6–8; Jeremiah 5:22; 8:7; Jonah 4:7; Matthew 5:45; 10:29.
source_text: XVII. Tertio, est generalis aut specialis. XVIII. Gubernatio GENERALIS est, qua Deus gubernat res universas communiter. Dicitur etiam universalis, item communis providentia. Et haec non admittit magis et minus. XIX. Gubernatio SPECIALIS est, qua Deus gubernat res singulas naturis ipsarum convenienter. Haec etiam singularis providentia appellatur; et suos quosdam gradus habet. XX. Estque creaturarum mere corporearum, aut corporearum incorporearumque simul, aut incorporearum simpliciter, sive angelorum et hominum. XXI. Mere corporeas creaturas Deus minus quidem operose, sic tamen gubernat ut, quod illis datum, in eo ipsas aut conservet, aut sublimet, aut deprimat; altera iterum regit ita expertes, altera ut sentientes. Confer Deuteronomy 28; Psalm 104; 146:6–9; Psalm 147 totum; Isaiah 42:5; Acts 14:15–17; Job 36–41; Proverbs 6:6–8; Jeremiah 5:22; 8:7; Jonah 4:7; Matthew 5:45; 10:29.
